payload.claim: spec_ids() treats any `.md` file directly under `.saffron/specs/` or `.saffron/specs/done/` as a spec and accepts the first line matching `^id:` anywhere in its text as a declared spec id, with no check that the file actually has YAML frontmatter. `.saffron/specs/done/README.md` matches the same pathspec and sits in that directory today; `_retired_ids` (saffron/scheduler.py:631-650) explicitly special-cases this file and only credits ids that parse as real spec frontmatter via `load_spec`, noting in its own docstring that README.md is 'a resident, not a broken spec.' The new function replicates none of that care: it would silently add any line beginning with `id:` in that README (or any other non-spec `.md` file later placed in those directories) to the known-id set, letting a cited id that is not actually a declared spec pass the new integrity check as if it were legitimate. It happens to be harmless today only because README.md currently contains no line starting with `id:`.
